voyage.title: Mungo Park on the Niger (1795-1797)
voyage.ships: on horseback and on foot, and finally with nothing at all
voyage.sponsor: sent by the African Association of London to find the course of the Niger
voyage.summary: Inland from the Gambia with two companions and a horse: imprisoned for four months by a Moorish chief, escaping alone across the Sahel, reaching the Niger at Segou to find it flowing east, and walking back destitute — carried the last stage by a slave caravan whose passage he recorded from inside it.
voyage.what_was_lost: Park kept notes throughout and lost most of them; the narrative was written up in London afterwards, for a society that had paid for it. The people who kept him alive appear mostly without names. And the coffle he travelled with on the return is described by the one man in it who was not for sale.

waypoints.event: Mungo Park departed from Portsmouth on his voyage to Africa, beginning the journey that would take him to the Gambia River and eventually into the interior in search of the Niger.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.place_modern: Pisania (near Karantaba, on the Gambia River), The Gambia

waypoints.event: Mungo Park entered Fatteconda, the capital of Bondou, crossing a river on horseback, and was soon invited to lodge with a respectable Slatee before being summoned to an audience with the king (Almami).
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.event: Mungo Park arrived at Teesee, in the Kingdom of Kasson, after crossing the Senegal, and was lodged in Demba Sego's hut; the next morning he was introduced to Tiggity Sego, brother to the King of Kasson and chief of Teesee.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.place_modern: Kamalia, Mali (near Sibidooloo/Manding region, present-day Mali)
waypoints.event: Mungo Park arrived at Kamalia in Manding country, exhausted and ill, and was received by the Bushreen slave-trader Karfa Taura, who was assembling a slave coffle to sell to Europeans on the Gambia and who hospitably took Park into his household.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.event: After many delays and postponed dates, Mungo Park's slave coffle finally departed Kamalia for the Gambia, with the townspeople following the caravan a short distance and performing a farewell ceremony on a rise overlooking the town.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.place_modern: Malakoota area on the Sénégal (Bafing) River, Guinea/Mali border region, West Africa
waypoints.event: Mungo Park's slave coffle, guided in part by the schoolmaster whose native town this was, sent a messenger ahead to arrange provisions before arriving at Malacotta, and later some slaves joined the coffle to continue on to Baniserile, the capital of Dentila.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.place_modern: Medina (Wuli region), Gambia River, The Gambia

waypoints.event: Mungo Park arrived at Pisania, a small British trading factory on the Gambia River established in the King of Yany's dominions, where he was accommodated by Dr. Laidley.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.event: After a harrowing Atlantic crossing from Gorée, Mungo Park's ship made for the West Indies to save the crew, striking the Diamond Rock before limping into St. John's harbour, Antigua; the vessel was condemned and the slaves aboard were reportedly sold. Park remained on the island about ten days before securing passage home.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)

waypoints.event: Mungo Park, having sailed from St. John's (Antigua) aboard the Chesterfield Packet on 24 November, arrived at Falmouth after a tempestuous voyage, completing his return from the interior of Africa, and set out immediately for London.
waypoints.diary_source_citation: Travels in the Interior Districts of Africa (Mungo Park, 1799)
